title: The Feist Function Is Not the Feistel Function: Disambiguation Matrix with Structural-Homology Annotation
author: Lee Sharks

version_history.note: Initial deposit. Disambiguation packet for Feist Function (Sharks 2026) vs Feistel Function (Feistel 1973). Includes empirical reception event (Bing collapse), 11-axis disambiguation matrix, structural-homology section surfacing genuine cousinhood, forensic canaries, JSON-LD schema, test queries.

creator: Lee Sharks
description:
This packet distinguishes the Feist Function, a literary voice-transformation protocol, from the Feistel function used in block-cipher design. It was produced after a reported Bing Chat answer resolved the rarer term into the more frequent cryptographic neighbor.

The matrix compares domain, origin, type signature, parameters, nonlinearity, preserved property, iteration, direction, examples, canaries, and verification. The Feist Function maps source text and declared literary parameters to an activated text. The Feistel structure operates on bitstrings and round subkeys to support an invertible cipher network.

The packet does not stop at difference. It proposes a structural homology: both can be represented as iterative transformations with per-round parameters and a property preserved across repeated application. Feistel structures preserve invertibility; the Feist protocol seeks to preserve break, seam, or voice pressure.

That relation should be described as analogy or formal homology, not common mathematical membership. The Feist Function’s “rounds” are not defined with the precision of cryptographic rounds, its parameters are literary heuristics, and its output lacks an objective test vector. Saying both are round functions is rhetorically useful but can reproduce the same category collapse the packet opposes.

The packet coins **sympathetic error** for a false identity produced by genuine resemblance plus frequency imbalance. This is the most transferable contribution: retrieval can detect a valid structural likeness and then incorrectly turn resemblance into identity.

wiki_article:
**The Feist Function Is Not the Feistel Function** is a disambiguation packet by Lee Sharks.

It separates a literary voice-recovery protocol from the cryptographic Feistel structure and compares them across eleven axes.

The packet also identifies a limited structural homology: both use repeated parameterized transformation, but they preserve different properties for different purposes.

The term **sympathetic error** names a retrieval mistake in which genuine resemblance contributes to a false merger.
